mapmc-fmc-2021-p2.title: Check each letter
mapmc-fmc-2021-p2.body:
A is only in the black circle, B only in the purple circle, E only in the red circle. C is in the black and red circles but not the purple one. D is in the middle where all three circles overlap.

**Answer: (D)**

mapmc-fmc-2021-01.title: Trace each entrance
mapmc-fmc-2021-01.body:
Trace a path from each entrance with your finger. Entrances B, C, D and E all lead to dead ends. Only the path from entrance A winds round and reaches the gap below the prize.

**Answer: (A)**

mapmc-fmc-2021-01.title: Work backwards from the prize
mapmc-fmc-2021-01.body:
Start at the prize and follow the only way out (the gap at the bottom of the inner box). Keep following the corridor outwards: it leads to entrance A.

**Answer: (A)**

mapmc-fmc-2021-02.title: Follow the keypad
mapmc-fmc-2021-02.body:
On the keypad, 0 is three rows straight below 2. So from 2 to 0 is *down three*. Then back to 2 is *up three*. Finally 1 is just left of 2: *left one*.

**Answer: (C) down three, up three, left one**

mapmc-fmc-2021-03.title: Odd times odd
mapmc-fmc-2021-03.body:
An answer is odd only when both numbers are odd. Of 2, 5 and 10, only 5 is odd. So only the box for $5 \times 5 = 25$ is odd: one box.

**Answer: (B) one**

mapmc-fmc-2021-04.title: Given out plus left
mapmc-fmc-2021-04.body:
Given out: $4 \times 3 = 12$ crayons. Left in the packet: 9. Full packet: $12 + 9 = 21$.

**Answer: (D) 21**

mapmc-fmc-2021-05.title: Look at each crossing
mapmc-fmc-2021-05.body:
Where two planks cross, the one you can see all of is on top.
- W is not covered by anything, so W is the top plank.
- V is covered wherever it crosses another plank, so V is the bottom plank.
- X lies across Y, so Y is below X.
- Z lies across X (and across Y), so Z is above X.

From the bottom: V, Y, X, Z, W.

**Answer: (E) VYXZW**

mapmc-fmc-2021-05.title: Use the options
mapmc-fmc-2021-05.body:
Only options A and E start with V (bottom) and end with W (top). They differ in the order of X and Z. Since Z lies on top of X, X must come first: VYXZW.

**Answer: (E) VYXZW**

mapmc-fmc-2021-06.title: One hour, then 20 minutes
mapmc-fmc-2021-06.body:
After 1 hour the minute hand goes all the way round and is back at 6. Each number on the clock is 5 minutes, so 20 minutes is 4 numbers: 7, 8, 9, 10.

**Answer: (E) 10**

mapmc-fmc-2021-07.title: Continue the pattern
mapmc-fmc-2021-07.body:
The shapes use 1, 4, 7, 10 matchsticks: 3 more each time. Shape 5 has 13 and shape 6 has 16.

**Answer: (A) 16**

mapmc-fmc-2021-07.title: A rule
mapmc-fmc-2021-07.body:
Shape 1 has 1 matchstick and each later shape adds 3. Shape 6 has $1 + 5 \times 3 = 16$.

**Answer: (A) 16**

mapmc-fmc-2021-08.title: Small, then bigger
mapmc-fmc-2021-08.body:
- The 6 coloured pieces are each a triangle: **6**.
- The diagonal from the top right to the bottom left corner cuts the rectangle into two big triangles: **2**.
- Two neighbouring pieces in the top half make a triangle twice: the top blue + yellow, and the yellow + left purple: **2**.
- In the bottom half, the blue + purple pieces make one more triangle: **1**.

Total: $6 + 2 + 2 + 1 = 11$.

**Answer: (D) 11**

mapmc-fmc-2021-09.title: Half of 40 minutes
mapmc-fmc-2021-09.body:
Halfway through 40 minutes is after 20 minutes. $09{:}15 + 20$ minutes $= 09{:}35$.

**Answer: (A) 09:35**

mapmc-fmc-2021-09.title: Find the end first
mapmc-fmc-2021-09.body:
The lesson ended at $09{:}15 + 40$ min $= 09{:}55$. Halfway between 09:15 and 09:55 is 09:35.

**Answer: (A) 09:35**

mapmc-fmc-2021-10.title: Think about the units digit
mapmc-fmc-2021-10.body:
Three Ys end in Y, so adding two more Ys to Y doesn't change the last digit: $Y + Y$ must end in 0. That happens for 0 and 5, and 0 can't make a two-digit answer, so $Y = 5$ ($5+5+5=15$).

**Answer: (B) 5**

mapmc-fmc-2021-11.title: Pairs that add to 15
mapmc-fmc-2021-11.body:
$7+8$ gives 56, $6+9$ gives 54 ✓, $5+10$ gives 50. So the numbers are 6 and 9.

**Answer: (E) 9**

mapmc-fmc-2021-12.title: Think in pairs
mapmc-fmc-2021-12.body:
Put each 5p with a 10p: each pair is 15p. £1.80 = 180p, and $180 \div 15 = 12$ pairs. 12 pairs is 24 coins.

**Answer: (D) 24**

mapmc-fmc-2021-12.title: Check the options
mapmc-fmc-2021-12.body:
The number of coins must be even (equal numbers of each). 24 coins: twelve 5p = 60p and twelve 10p = 120p, total 180p ✓.

**Answer: (D) 24**

mapmc-fmc-2021-13.title: Count up in 35s
mapmc-fmc-2021-13.body:
4 metres = 400 cm. $35 \times 10 = 350$, $35 \times 11 = 385$, $35 \times 12 = 420$ (too much). So 11 balloons, with 15 cm left over.

**Answer: (B) 11**

mapmc-fmc-2021-14.title: Rule out
mapmc-fmc-2021-14.body:
2022, 2024 and 2026 are even, so they are in the 2 times table. 2025 ends in 5, so it is in the 5 times table. 2023 is odd (so not in the 2 or 4 tables), does not end in 0 or 5, and $2 + 0 + 2 + 3 = 7$ is not a multiple of 3.

**Answer: (B) 2023**

mapmc-fmc-2021-15.title: Work each out
mapmc-fmc-2021-15.body:
- A: $23\frac12 + 2 = 25\frac12$ (1½ away)
- B: $29\frac12 - 3 = 26\frac12$ (½ away)
- C: $84 \div 3 = 28$ (1 away)
- D: $8 \times 3 = 24$ (3 away)
- E: half of 58 is 29 (2 away)

**Answer: (B)**

mapmc-fmc-2021-16.title: Perimeter, then share
mapmc-fmc-2021-16.body:
Rectangle perimeter: $10 + 8 + 10 + 8 = 36$ cm. A square has 4 equal sides: $36 \div 4 = 9$ cm.

**Answer: (A) 9 cm**

mapmc-fmc-2021-16.title: Half the perimeter
mapmc-fmc-2021-16.body:
Half the rectangle's perimeter is $10 + 8 = 18$ cm, which is two sides of the square. One side is $18 \div 2 = 9$ cm.

**Answer: (A) 9 cm**

mapmc-fmc-2021-18.title: Bar model in eighths
mapmc-fmc-2021-18.body:
Split all the apples into 8 equal parts. Ravi has 4 parts, Samina 1 part, Toby 1 part and 10 more. That makes 6 parts and 10 apples, so the other 2 parts must be the 10 apples. One part is 5 apples, and all 8 parts are 40.

**Answer: (D) 40**

mapmc-fmc-2021-18.title: Try the options
mapmc-fmc-2021-18.body:
The total must split into eighths, so of the options only 40 is possible (10, 20, 30 and 50 cannot be divided by 8). Check 40: Ravi 20, Samina 5, Toby $5 + 10 = 15$. $20 + 5 + 15 = 40$ ✓.

**Answer: (D) 40**

mapmc-fmc-2021-19.title: Boys only
mapmc-fmc-2021-19.body:
Boys: $22 - 13 = 9$. Boys with glasses: $7 - 5 = 2$. Boys without glasses: $9 - 2 = 7$.

**Answer: (B) 7**

mapmc-fmc-2021-19.title: Table
mapmc-fmc-2021-19.body:
| | glasses | no glasses | total |
|---|---|---|---|
| girls | 5 | 8 | 13 |
| boys | 2 | **7** | 9 |
| total | 7 | 15 | 22 |

**Answer: (B) 7**

mapmc-fmc-2021-20.title: Count the gaps
mapmc-fmc-2021-20.body:
Between the 1st and the 15th rider there are 14 gaps of 10 seconds: $14 \times 10 = 140$ seconds = 2 minutes 20 seconds.

**Answer: (C) 2 minutes 20 seconds**

mapmc-fmc-2021-20.title: Count the starts
mapmc-fmc-2021-20.body:
Rider 1 starts at 0 s, rider 2 at 10 s, rider 3 at 20 s … rider $n$ at $(n-1) \times 10$ s. Rider 15 starts at 140 s = 2 min 20 s.

**Answer: (C) 2 minutes 20 seconds**
